topicCandidates: Dependent as a supported-spouse-or-child activity route tied to an eligible principal status, with the current sponsor-status list, financial support, cohabitation or family-life evidence, individually designated period, and separate outside-activity permission.

Spouse or Child of Japanese National and Spouse or Child of Permanent Resident as distinct status-based routes whose child definitions are not interchangeable and whose spouse cases require an ongoing genuine marital relationship.
Long-Term Resident as a notification-based or individually recognized status for specified special circumstances, not a general fallback after divorce, family change, or long residence.

Permanent Residence under the February 24, 2026 guideline, including the ordinary residence rule, route-specific exceptions, public obligations, current-status compliance, guarantor and evidence paths, pending-application obligations, and the maximum-period treatment changing April 1, 2027.
Designated Activities as an umbrella whose permitted work, family accompaniment, period, renewal, and transition are controlled by the exact designation rather than the English status label.

Continued job hunting after Japanese study, including covered graduates, school recommendation and continuing search evidence, ordinary time limits, qualifying local-government support, outside-activity permission, and the separate job-offer waiting route.

J-Find for recent graduates of currently qualifying overseas universities: ranking-list and graduation timing, degree, age, initial funds, job-search or business-preparation activity, family, cumulative program time, and transition planning.

Digital Nomad Designated Activities: covered nationality or citizenship, foreign-facing remote work, income and insurance thresholds, six-month non-renewable stay, six-month wait before reuse, family, local-client prohibition, tax-treaty uncertainty, and absence of a residence card.

Long-stay sightseeing and recreation: visa-waiver nationality or citizenship, age, savings ownership and history, insurance, accompanying-spouse conditions, exclusion of children and work, six-month grant, and possible extension up to one year.

Medical Stay as a coordinated visa and residence decision: short treatment, multiple-entry medical visa, hospitalization beyond ninety days, Designated Activities for the patient and attendant, guarantor or medical coordinator, treatment and financing evidence, and no remunerative activity for the attendant.

Working Holiday as a bilateral, holiday-first Designated Activities program with country-specific age, residence, quota, funds, insurance, participation-count, work, prohibited-industry, and application rules rather than one global checklist.

Temporary Visitor as a short activity category distinct from visa exemption or eVISA eligibility, with nationality and passport conditions, 15-, 30-, or 90-day landing periods, no remunerative activity, exceptional extension rules, and no ordinary resident onboarding.

Diplomat and Official as assignment- and recognition-based routes coordinated through governments, missions, or recognized international organizations; passport type alone does not establish either status and private travel may instead be Temporary Visitor.
userSituations: A professional or student wants to bring a spouse, child, parent, unmarried partner, or other relative and assumes every principal status supports Dependent.
A spouse on Dependent wants part-time or full-time work and needs to distinguish outside-activity permission from obtaining an independent work status.
A family member is choosing among Dependent, Spouse or Child of Japanese National, Spouse or Child of Permanent Resident, and Long-Term Resident based on the exact relationship and sponsor position.

A child is born in Japan and the parents need to distinguish nationality, municipal birth registration, status acquisition, and the narrow born-in-Japan child rule for Spouse or Child of Permanent Resident.

A marriage ends through divorce, bereavement, separation, or domestic violence and the resident needs urgent notification and route-change guidance without being told that Long-Term Resident is automatic.

A resident is preparing for Permanent Residence and needs the ordinary or exceptional residence timeline, timely tax and social-insurance record, current period-of-stay rule, and continued extension of the present status while the application is pending.
A former international student continues a pre-graduation job search, joins a qualifying local support program, receives a future job offer, or considers J-Find and needs the routes kept separate.
A recent overseas graduate checks J-Find using an outdated university ranking list or assumes its two years are independent of time used under certain similar programs.
A remote worker has Japanese clients, a Japanese employment offer, a spouse or child, or plans repeated stays and needs the Digital Nomad boundaries stated before travel.
A financially self-supported visitor compares ordinary Temporary Visitor, long-stay sightseeing, Digital Nomad, and a relocation status.
A patient compares a short medical visit, repeated treatment trips, and hospitalization exceeding ninety days while an accompanying person needs a legally accurate route and work boundary.
A young traveler checks Working Holiday eligibility after recent bilateral changes and needs the rules for their nationality and application location rather than a generic age promise.
A diplomatic or official passport holder travels privately, accompanies an assigned household member, or changes assignment and needs coordination with the sending organization and Japanese mission.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: Dependent currently covers the supported spouse or child of listed principal statuses, including Specified Skilled Worker (ii), but not Specified Skilled Worker (i). A parent, sibling, unmarried partner, or adult independent child does not become eligible merely through financial support.

Dependent does not authorize ordinary employment. Blanket outside-activity permission may allow up to twenty-eight hours weekly under its conditions, but a full-time career generally requires an appropriate independent status or a distinct special-family provision.

The child categories differ: Spouse or Child of Japanese National includes a person born as a child of a Japanese national and a qualifying special adoptee, while Spouse or Child of Permanent Resident covers a biological child born in Japan who continued residing in Japan. These are not generic dependent-child labels.

Status-based residence ordinarily has no activity restriction, but the relationship or position supporting a spouse status must remain genuine for renewal. Divorce or bereavement triggers a fourteen-day notification for covered spouse holders.

Six months without spouse activity can create revocation risk, but domestic violence, child-rearing, litigation, unavoidable separation, or other justifiable reasons require careful treatment. The guide must not tell a person in danger to remain with an abusive spouse.

Long-Term Resident includes notification categories and discretionary individual cases. Prior marriage to a Japanese or permanent resident, years lived in Japan, or custody of a child is relevant evidence in some cases but never an automatic entitlement.

Permanent Residence is a separate permission, not an extension. A pending application does not extend the current period of stay, so the applicant must separately maintain and renew the present status when necessary.

The February 24, 2026 Permanent Residence guideline continues temporary treatment of a three-year period as the longest period only through March 31, 2027, with limited transitional handling for certain holders thereafter. This must be effective-dated rather than stated as a timeless three-year rule.

Designated Activities does not carry one work rule. A Working Holiday designation may allow incidental work, Digital Nomad permits defined foreign-facing remote work, long-stay sightseeing prohibits work, and continued job hunting requires separate outside-activity permission for part-time work.

Continued job hunting is not available to every graduate or every post-graduation search. Covered institution, course, credential, continuity of job hunting, school recommendation, finances, and relation to a prospective work status matter.

Waiting after receiving a job offer is a separate Designated Activities situation. Current guidance uses both an offer-to-start limit and a graduation-to-start limit and requires employer contact and cancellation undertakings.

J-Find uses the currently published eligible-university basis, graduation within five years, a degree, age eighteen or older, and initial funds. Its maximum two-year period can interact with time used under listed similar job-hunting or entrepreneurial-preparation programs.

Digital Nomad is six months with no extension and no residence card. It does not authorize employment or comparable contracting with a Japanese public or private organization, and a tax treaty—not the immigration label alone—controls any income-tax exemption.

Long-stay sightseeing normally begins with six months and can reach at most one year through an eligible extension. Children cannot accompany under that scheme, and spouses staying separately create a higher combined savings requirement.

A Medical Stay visa is not itself one uniform status of residence. Treatment of ninety days or less can use a short-stay framework, while hospitalization exceeding ninety days requires the longer Designated Activities analysis and a COE route.

Working Holiday eligibility and repeat participation changed for several partner countries and Taiwan between December 2024 and February 2026. Country-specific embassy rules, quotas, and prohibited employment must be checked at application time.

Visa exemption, eVISA availability, visa validity, and the Temporary Visitor period granted at landing are separate concepts. Short stay never authorizes remunerative activity merely because a visa was waived.

Diplomatic or official passport possession does not alone produce Diplomat or Official status. Private tourism can result in Temporary Visitor treatment, and visa-exemption arrangements differ by passport and nationality.

Diplomat, Official, Temporary Visitor, and Digital Nomad holders are outside the ordinary mid-to-long-term residence-card system; shared arrival guidance must not automatically send them through residence-card and municipal resident-registration steps.
jurisdictionVariables: The principal resident's exact status, the family relationship recognized under the applicable route, dependency, household facts, age, place of birth, continued residence, and evidence from every relevant civil registry.

Nationality and family law, Japanese family-register records, foreign marriage or birth documents, translation, legalization or authentication, and same-sex-marriage or non-marital-partner facts requiring route-specific official advice.
The resident's current status, period, address, tax, pension, health-insurance, criminal, notification, travel, and compliance record for renewal or Permanent Residence.
The exact Designated Activities notification number or individual designation printed in the person's designated-activities record, not merely the status name on a residence card.

Current eligible countries, passport type, bilateral arrangement, application residence, age, quota, funds, insurance, permitted work, and repeat-participation rule for visitor, digital-nomad, and Working Holiday routes.

The education provider, credential, graduation date, pre-graduation search activity, recommendation, local-government support program, job offer, anticipated start date, and prospective work-status fit for graduate routes.
The medical purpose, expected treatment and hospitalization duration, single or repeated visits, host institution, registered guarantor, accompanying-person need, financing, and treatment plan.

The sending government or international organization, Japanese recognition, assignment purpose, household relationship, note verbale, passport, privileges or immunities, and whether the trip is official or private.
Tax, social insurance, family law, employment, professional licensing, public benefits, and municipal processes that remain separate from immigration permission.

scopeBoundaries: Do not use family visa as though it were one legal route. Name the exact status and relationship or principal-status basis.

Do not determine whether a foreign marriage, same-sex marriage, adoption, parent-child relationship, domestic partnership, or custody arrangement is legally recognized from a short questionnaire; identify the document and authority checks required.
Do not imply that marriage, birth, sponsorship, divorce, bereavement, domestic violence, years in Japan, or child custody automatically grants, preserves, changes, or cancels a status.
Do not present Long-Term Resident as a general humanitarian or post-divorce fallback. Explain published categories and examples while preserving individual review.

Do not predict Permanent Residence approval from years alone or collapse the ordinary, spouse or child, Long-Term Resident, highly skilled, contribution, refugee, and other exceptions into one timeline.
Do not say that a pending Permanent Residence application protects an expiring current status, and do not publish the temporary three-year treatment without its April 2027 effective-date boundary.
Do not assign one period, renewal rule, work permission, family rule, or evidence list to all Designated Activities. The exact designation controls.
Do not treat J-Find, continued job hunting, waiting after a job offer, Start-up, or ordinary work status as interchangeable because each can involve job or business preparation.
Do not imply that Digital Nomad authorizes Japanese employment or clients, that long-stay sightseeing permits remote work, or that a tax treaty automatically exempts every remote worker.
Do not describe a Medical Stay visa, Temporary Visitor, and Designated Activities medical stay as the same legal permission.
Do not copy one Working Holiday country's age, quota, funds, insurance, or participation rule to every partner.
Do not infer Diplomat or Official status from a passport label; assignment purpose and Japanese recognition control.
Keep family law, nationality, tax, insurance, employment, healthcare, professional licensing, diplomatic privileges, and municipal obligations separate from immigration permission.
Keep every materially revised or new guide at needs-review until explicit human editorial approval.
